newsitem.title: USA: ITT seen selling all but Sheraton, Caesars.
newsitem.headline: ITT seen selling all but Sheraton, Caesars.

text.p: ITT Corp, in rejecting Hilton Hotel Corp's takeover offer, will likely sell all assets except Sheraton and Caesars in a bid to hone its focus and boost shareholder value, traders and money managers said.
"They're going to sell anything not having to do with hotels and gaming," said Steve Cohen, a partner at the New York-based money management firm Kellner, DiLeo & Co.
ITT, which earlier rebuffed Hilton's $55-a-share bid, was trading at 56-7/8, up 7/8 in the U.S. pre-open. Hilton was unchanged at Tuesday's close of 28-1/8.

An ITT spokesman would only say that the company will focus on continuing to build its gaming and lodging businesses. ITT Wednesday rejected Hilton's offer, calling the offer inadequate and not in the best interests of its shareholders.

Cohen and others said the company will likely be left with only its ITT Sheraton hotel and Caesars World gaming assets after monetizing or spining off non-core assets like Madison Square Garden, the New York Knicks, New York Rangers and ITT educational properties.
Officials from Hilton were not immediately available to comment on whether Hilton would boost its bid for ITT.
When asked what ITT would do if Hilton sweetened its offer, the ITT spokesman said, "We will see what happens," and added, "We have no comment now on anything Hilton will do."
Traders said ITT might use proceeds from a sale of its non-core assets to buy back stock, initiate a self-tender offer or further invest in Caesars and Sheraton.
They said that all of these actions, however, depend on how much ITT received from the assets' sale. They said making an estimate on how much the assets would bring in was difficult at this point.
"The real question is will ITT get a good price for their holdings," one trader, who asked his name not be used, said.
"It might be embarrassing for them if they don't get a good price for something like Madison Square Garden, because they paid a lot for it."
-- Jeff Mamera in the New York newsroom 212-859-1700
